instructions: Put the 1 cup toor dal in a medium pot and cover it with cold water. Rub the dal between your hands, then drain. Repeat about 3 times, until the water runs almost clear.
Add 4 cups fresh water to the pot and bring it to a boil over high heat. Scoop off any foam that rises.

Partly cover the pot and simmer on medium low for 40 to 50 minutes, stirring now and then, until the dal is completely soft and falls apart when you press it against the side of the pot. Add 1/2 cup hot water if it gets thick before it's soft.
Meanwhile, finely chop the onion and the 3 tomatoes and finely chop the ginger. Finely chop all 7 garlic cloves and keep them in two piles: 4 cloves for the masala and 3 for the tadka.
Seed and thinly slice the green chili into a small bowl for the table, and cut the lemon into wedges. Chop a small handful of the cilantro.

When the dal is soft, mash it lightly with a whisk or the back of a spoon, leaving some of it whole. It should pour like a thick soup. Stir in a splash of hot water if it's thicker than that, and keep it on low.
Heat the 2 tbsp oil in a large skillet over medium. Add 1/2 tsp of the cumin seeds. After about 20 seconds they'll sizzle and turn a shade darker. That's your cue for the onion.
Add the onion and cook for 5 to 6 minutes, stirring now and then, until it's soft and golden at the edges.
Stir in the ginger and the 4 cloves of garlic and cook for about 1 minute, until they smell fragrant.
Turn the heat to low and stir in the 1/4 tsp turmeric, 1/2 tsp of the chili powder and the 1/2 tsp garam masala. Stir for about 20 seconds.
Add the tomatoes and the 1 tsp salt. Cook for 5 to 6 minutes, stirring, until the tomatoes are soft and mushy.
Scrape the masala into the pot of dal and stir it in. Simmer gently for 6 to 7 minutes.
Crush the 1 tbsp kasuri methi between your palms over the pot, stir in the chopped cilantro and turn off the heat.
For the tadka, heat the 2 tbsp ghee in a small pan over medium. Add the last 1/2 tsp cumin seeds and let them sizzle for about 20 seconds.
Add the 2 dried chilies and the 3 cloves of garlic and stir for about 1 minute, until the garlic turns pale gold. Don't let it brown.
Take the pan off the heat and stir in the pinch of asafoetida and the last 1/4 tsp chili powder. Pour it straight over the dal. It will sizzle.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt or a squeeze of the lemon.
Serve with basmati rice or roti, with the lemon wedges and sliced chili on the side.
method_notes: Both versions cook toor dal until it's soft, stir it into an onion, ginger, garlic and tomato masala with kasuri methi and cilantro, and finish with a ghee tadka of cumin, dried red chilies, garlic, asafoetida and chili powder. Swasthi's (the lead) uses turmeric and garam masala in the masala and serves it with lemon. Cook with Manali also blooms coriander seeds and cloves, cooks the tomatoes covered and adds a charcoal smoke at the end. Both pressure cook the dal; this one simmers it on the stove, which takes longer, softens the onion before the garlic and ginger go in, and puts the green chili on the side.
